about: The measured half of docs/03-quality-bar.md, as numbers a machine can check.
Every entry carries the film and the reaction that set it. A metric with no recorded
failure behind it does not belong in this file: a threshold nobody was ever rejected on
is a preference, and preferences drift into gates that block good work.
Severity is 'fail' only where a delivery was actually sent back or a rule was stated as
hard. Where the archive records a target AND a shipped film that passed it by, the entry
is a 'warn' and says so. Do not promote a warn to a fail without a rejection to cite.
One entry is marked derived:true. Read its note before trusting the exact number.
Read with tools/qa/benchmark.py. Prose and provenance: docs/03-quality-bar.md,

note: Both are on the MAX GRID CELL mean absolute luma difference between samples taken
10 times a second at 180x320, not on the whole-frame mean. The whole-frame mean is the
same mistake the contrast gate made: it averages a real local event down to nothing.
Calibrated against four delivered films. The whole-frame mean reports vid62-short at
29% frozen; the cell max reports 15%, and 15% is what its held runs actually add up to.

why: A 4K container carrying a 1080p face shipped three times. The transcode step said
scale=1080:1920 while the compositions render at 2160x3840, so a 4K master was
downscaled and then upscaled back by the renderer. Rasterising the same frame from
each asset: 1080 asset 6.51 Laplacian variance, 2160 asset 11.99, the master 12.58.
84% sharper from the native asset. Right resolution, wrong detail, and every
resolution check you can think to run passes. Triggered by the creator's one-line
question, 'is this video rendered in the same file size that I gave you the a
roll as'.
Match the asset to the composition's OUTPUT: 1080 stays correct for a client short
that genuinely outputs 1080x1920, and vid33 v9 recorded the opposite trap, comparing
against the camera's 4K when the render target was a 1080x1920 Reel.
vid60 shipped 2160x3840 from a 2160x3840 master with the asset chain correct and
the creator said 'it is very much compressed'. `-q high` picked 15.5 Mbps against
the master's 28.0, about half what a modern phone writes. Re-rendered at 28.3 Mbps
it cost 2m46s and bought +13.2% high-frequency detail in the face region.
vid55 shipped the raw render at 29,314,793 bytes and came back with 'the size of this
video is very low, need it to be in the actual size of my a roll or more than that,
how tf it is so low, we decided it to be on that size itself'. Re-delivered at
118,711,758 bytes, delta zero.
CRF cannot be the contract: vid61 round 1 landed 36.8 Mbps at --crf 10 and round 2
landed 24.9 at the same CRF, because three drawn artboards were replaced by one dark
screen recording. Pin the rate, not the quality.
On record: vid59 38.4 against 43.9, vid60 v5 28.3 against 28.0, vid61 36.8 against
Pass the CAMERA master, not the project's CRF-17 transcode. hf67/assets/aroll.mp4
carries 43.2 Mbps against the 33.15 Mbps master it was made from, so using it as the
reference turns a 1.16x pass into a 0.89x fail.
Two competing correct answers, which is why this is a wide warn and not a target.
The house delivery pass is two-pass loudnorm to -14.5 LUFS / -1.0 dBTP for Instagram
and -14 for YouTube: vid36 went -16.7 to -14.8, vid41's mix arrived at -19.0 and
shipped at -14.8, vid47 came off the renderer at -19.5 and shipped at -14.5.
The counter-rule is stronger on the creators who hand over a finished mix. vid57's
delivery script loudnorms to -14 as its first step and that is audio processing the
creator vetoed; the render mix was -21.83 and shipped there. vid63 delivered -21.2
against that master's -21.6 deliberately.
So a reading near -14.5 on those accounts means the vetoed pass ran, and a reading
near -22 on an account that normalises means the pass was skipped. Neither is
readable from the number alone. audio.lufs_delta_vs_master is the check with teeth.
'I really don't want to touch my A-roll at any given cost.' The delivery script
loudnorms to -14 LUFS as step 1 and that is audio processing the creator vetoed for
that film; a --raw-audio path was added for it. The render mix measured -21.83
against the source's -22.25, the 0.4 dB being the SFX bed. vid63 delivered -21.2
against a -21.6 master. vid67: the VO -22.6 LUFS in, -22.5 out.
SKIPPED when the master has no audio track, which is the case for a video-only
transcoded asset, and skipped on the accounts that normalise to an absolute target.
vid38's mix measured a comfortable -12.6 LUFS integrated at +4.7 dBTP: a VO whose own
peak is -1.0 dBFS plus about 38 SFX clips sums past full scale even at 0.16 to 0.26
volumes. It recurred at +4.1 on vid42 and +4.0 on vid43, which is where the file says
the two-pass loudnorm with -c:v copy 'is not optional on this SFX-dense grammar'.
Integrated loudness and true peak fail independently and only the second one clips in
a phone speaker. It costs no video time.
One documented exception, and check for it before acting: on a film where the owner
said the mix is final, volumedetect max 0.0 dBFS was CORRECT, a single transient and
not sustained clipping. Confirm with astats Flat factor 0.000 and Abs Peak count.
'Nothing static for more than about 1 second' has been in the grammar since vid2 and
nothing checked it until motion_guard. vid56's short round 1 held 10.0s, 23% of the
cut, with runs of 3.6s, 3.8s and 4.8s, and drew 'the animation is very still here'.
Severity is warn on purpose: a held frame can be deliberate, and vid58's round 2 kept
two 1.6s breaths in a cut that was accepted. The point is that the decision gets made
on purpose instead of discovered by the client.
This measures literally frozen PIXELS, a strict subset of the DOM-side held blocks
motion_guard reports, so any breach here is a certain breach of the rule.
The recorded rejections are on the DOM-side measure, not on pixels: vid59 at 66% held
drew 'very boring b roll' and 'need better animations'; vid62 round 1 measured 71%
with a longest hold of 17.0s and drew 'only a text-based thing is really too shitty',
rebuilt onto word onsets to 56% then 35%; vid58's short measured 86% on its first
pass and 7% on the round that shipped. The stated target is 40% or under, and vid62
did not meet it: 'closing the rest would mean decorating every 2 to 3s gap, which is
its own defect'.
That 40% is NOT portable to this metric. A frozen-pixel run is a strict subset of a
DOM held block, so the same films measure far lower here and 40% would never trip.
0.10 is calibrated against four delivered films (vid67 0%, vid63 2%, the fast-cut-ad
demo film 6%, vid62-short 15%) and is the one number in this file that is a
derivation rather than
a recorded rejection. It stays a warn until a film is rejected at a known pixel-side
figure. If you want the number the rejections were actually written against, run
the DOM-side guard on the composition.
The creator sent back a frame with 'What the fuck is this?'. Content stopped at
y1530 and the bottom 390px, 20% of the frame, averaged 13/255, with a pure-black
seam at y1000 to y1040 where the face band's feather ran to solid. The creator
reviews the exported 9:16 file in a player, where an unlit reserved zone reads as a
broken black bar rather than as
a reserved zone. A wide shallow stage lift along the floor took the band to 28.5 mean
and softened the seam to 7.0.
Reserving a zone means keeping TEXT out of it, never leaving it black. Related and
separately recorded: a split band that stops at y1580 leaves 340px of bare paper, and
the reserved zone protects the presenter's CHIN, not their chest.
Meaningful on 9:16 only. On a 16:9 long-form there is no Instagram band to reserve.
0.14 is the ink floor tools/gates/guard.py already enforces per graphics zone, set
after three vid61 scenes spent 0.8 to 1.8s as one element at the top of an 1120px
column over blank paper. They passed lint, they passed validate, the motion guard saw
plenty of movement and the safe-zone gate saw nothing out of bounds. A frame can be
moving, in-bounds and contrast-safe while two thirds of it is blank.
Applied here to frame 0 because frame 0 is the Reels cover and a delivered asset in
its own right. vid49 records the sharper version of the same point: the grid preview
crops to 4:5, y285 to y1635, and v1's eyebrow at y150 and hook number at y194 were
both above it, so 'the thumbnail lost the entire claim'. This metric sees an empty
cover. It cannot see a cover whose ink is all outside the 4:5 crop, so look at frame
0 as well as measuring it.
y1600 of 1920 is where Instagram's bottom UI band starts, and 'a talking-head chin
below about 1600 is a guaranteed re-edit request' is one of the oldest rules here.
Above the chin IS the face: vid46's short reasoned a redaction stack at y1000 to
y1346 as 'the chest' and a ruler overlay put y1000 on the presenter's nose and
y1346 on their lower lip.
vid60's chin was measured at 11 points over 29 seconds, worst case y1080, and a plate
placed at y1190 off that number rendered across the presenter's neck: they lean in at
the CTA and the chin there is y1145, collar y1280. A sparse sample of a talking head
measures the pose they hold, not the pose they move into. Measure the WINDOW the beat
uses.
Read contourBot, not the bounding box. On vid62 the landmark itself was wrong three
times: the true crown sits 441px above the face bbox top, and under the shipped
transform the presenter's head was cut off in essentially every carded frame while
the gate reported 28%.
Passes on record: vid67 chin max 1548.7, vid59's short worst band chin y1519, vid58's
short worst y1511. Coincidences on record: 25px of clearance on vid58's p97 and 24px
on vid59's, both of which the archive calls a coincidence and not a margin.
'Remove the double em dashes from text wherever they are, and make sure you don't add
any', stated on the longform-chunked account and recorded as applying to ALL videos;
it is a standing rule on card-reel, paper-split and fast-cut-ad too. vid46 round 3
swept 13 on-screen instances and 14
in the caption pack. Label separators become the house middot, sentence dashes become
a comma or a colon.
It is a PRE-RENDER check, not a pre-delivery one: seven `FIG. NN` labels found late
cost a full 4K re-render on vid52.
And it was only ever enforced inside the composition, so the deliverables were never
scanned: 19 delivered caption packs and 2 delivered SRTs in out/ carry em dashes,
vid58's pack 14 of them and vid62-short's 11. Pass --srt, --caption-pack and
--composition or this check measures nothing, which is exactly how it shipped broken
21 times.
Both edges have a rejection. Too little: vid42 v2 went 27% to 44% on 'need to show
my face for like 11.5 seconds at the very start'. Too much: 'no need to show my
face from here, just show the animations and the content in the full screen', and
'no need to show my face too much, only at important lines and with split screen'.
The shape that landed is a 1.4s full-bleed open then card beats at the important
lines: vid42 v3 at 30% with four card beats reads as 'present throughout', two did
not, and vid63 shipped at 46% (13.9s of 30.1) with never a full-bleed beat.
Vision misses profiles and occluded jaws, so the measured number is a floor on the
real one. Treat a reading near an edge as a prompt to open the contact sheet.
The creator's mix ships untouched, so their films land where their master lands:
vid63 -21.2 against a -21.6 master, vid67 -22.5 out from -22.6 in, vid57's render
mix -21.83 against a -22.25 source. A card-reel film reading near -14.5 means the
loudnorm the creator vetoed ran. This band is descriptive;
audio.lufs_delta_vs_master has the teeth.
'We just can't show text, show animations while the man is also visible.' The reel
opens already in the split with a story running in the graphics zone, so the
presenter is on screen nearly throughout. vid47 v1 shipped at 45% face share on a
FACE/GFX/GFX
cadence and the note was 'we need to show the face more': v2 went to 91%. Earlier
cuts on this account run 40% and 70%, and the round that replaced the full-width
band with the floating card took 27% to 44%.
A low reading here means the split collapsed somewhere, which is a layout bug and
not a pacing choice.
Both behaviours are on record for this account and the difference is which layer.
The A-ROLL ships untouched: 'whatever there is in the video, mirrored or without
mirrored, keep that the same', and a pre-cut take at -25.9 dB mean shipped as is.
The delivery MIX was normalised on vid41 (-19.0 in, -14.8 out) and vid47 (-19.5 in,
-14.5 / -1.2 out) and both were accepted. Wide band, and read audio.true_peak_dbtp
instead: that is the one with a rejection behind it.
The self-mixed VO around -21 to -25 dB mean is also why the house SFX range of 0.16
to 0.34 overpowers it and this account's own band is 0.10 to 0.19.
The file-size matching rule is the two Instagram creators' rule and it explicitly
does NOT apply here: this account is 3840x2160 YouTube long-form and its cutdowns
are crops of it, so a whole-frame data rate against the master compares two
different pictures. vid62's short delivered 28.16 Mbps at 1080x1920 against a 32.78
Mbps 3840x2160 master, which reads 0.86x and means nothing.
What still applies here is not shipping a compressed-looking file: vid59 round 1
went out at 26.7 Mbps and was re-rendered at 38.4 against a 43.9 master.
Two-pass loudnorm to -14 LUFS / -1.0 dBTP for YouTube, and the cutdowns ship at the
same number: vid59's short delivered -14.0 / -0.9 and vid62's short delivered -14.0.
This is the account where the absolute figure is the working contract, because the
audio is rebuilt in the edit (source-aligned VO plus a separately-built SFX bed)
rather than stream-copied from a mix the creator made. No film on this account was
ever sent back on loudness, so it is a warn: the number is the practice, not a
rejection.
Not a contract on this account. Its delivery is normalised to an absolute target,
so a delta against the master is information and not a gate.
'Better A-rolls and more A-rolls' from the creator means b-roll, not face time,
confirmed directly: face share fell 43.2% to 39.4% in a round they approved.
Gaze-driven safe coverage on this account's long-forms runs 38% (vid44), 43%
The floor exists because of the opposite note: 'no need to show any animation here
... just the A-roll should be shown', said on a 4.6s closing beat that was
graphics-only with no face at all, and the creator said explicitly it generalises.
The precondition on the floor: the presenter reads from notes for about 45% of a
long take and showing them reading is a hard failure, so an unusable span comes off
the screen rather than getting smaller. Run tools/vision/gaze-detect.swift, not
taste, and
note that eyelid aperture alone cannot see gaze DIRECTION: at the two moments the
client flagged it read 0.347 and 0.361 against a film median of 0.379.
Downgraded to a warn because this account's primary format is 16:9 YouTube
long-form, where
there is no Instagram bottom band to reserve and this number is just whatever the
bottom sixth of the picture happens to be. Dark footage there would trip a hard
floor for no reason.
It is still the real check on its 9:16 cutdowns and it is not decorative: vid62's
short measures 22.9, above the 13.4 that drew the complaint and well below the
28.5 that answered it. Read this row against the format you are shipping.
This number reversed inside one production and it is the clearest example in the
archive of a round-scoped correction that is not law. Read both halves before
acting on the row.
Round 1: 'i really want this a fast paced edit for meta ads, plz make a note of it',
said after a first plan came in at a 2.28s mean shot modelled on the Wispr Flow
reference ads. The reference ads set the grammar, not the tempo. The plan landed at
42 shots over 36.2s, 0.86s mean, 1.46s longest, and the density came from
pre-rendered static crop-cuts of the 4K master, hard-cut to. A cut to a tighter
framing is not a camera move, and animating a scale on a <video> wrapper both reads
as a zoom and deadlocks the capture engine.
Rounds 6, 9 and 10 walked it back. Block E went from 7 shots to 3 held shots on
'let the b-roll breathe', and v17 confirmed two long b-roll holds beat three medium
ones: drop a shot rather than compress three. Then 'smooth and subtle but so
elegant' was measured against the reference the client named, a 79s Viktor ad with
zero cuts detectable at a 5% scene-change threshold, overlays fading in and HOLDING
for
5 to 10s. The translation was to kill the flash cuts and replace every back.out and
expo.out with 0.4 to 0.5s power2 fade-drifts.
So a fast-cut-ad cut measuring well above 1.5s is not automatically wrong. Ask which
grammar is live before you cut anything, and record the answer in HISTORY.md.
Two carve-outs held throughout: a beat where the viewer must READ product UI gets
0.9 to 1.3s, and the direct-ask CTA line stays on the presenter's face.
MEASUREMENT CAVEAT, read this before acting on the number. Mean shot length is the
least trustworthy row in the report and no detector threshold fixes it. The
fast-cut-ad demo film's density comes from static crop-cuts of the same person
against the same wall,
which barely score as scene changes: the plan is 42 shots over 36.2s and the
detector sees 11 at scene 0.25, 16 at 0.10 and 19 at 0.06, while the same sweep
takes vid63 from a correct 10 to 66 false cuts. The shot count lives in the shot
plan. Use this row to notice a cut that is nowhere near its plan, not to grade it.
v1 was rejected on two structural faults and one of them was the presenter's face
on screen 66% of the time; the other was abstract graphics instead of the client's
real interface. Both
were structural, so the cut was rebuilt from the shot spec rather than iterated.
The rebuild came back at about 14% full-frame (6.3s of 43.6s) plus 10.8s as a small
card beside the product. These are paid Meta placements: the product has to be on
screen, not the presenter.

audio.integrated_lufs.film: the fast-cut-ad demo film, the fast-cut-ad UGC reel
why: The A-roll audio is stream-copied bit for bit on this account: no denoise, no EQ, no
loudnorm, no grade on the picture either. Video 1 landed at -13.9 LUFS integrated
and the fast-cut-ad demo film's music sits about -13.9 dB at t=0.
Zero added sound effects here until asked. 'Remove the typing sfx' meant every added
sound and it took five rounds to learn: three evidence-based fixes removed the
click and tick family, then the music's own metronomic 0.465s percussion grid, then
the 2ms-attack reveal cues, and round 5's five timestamped notes (14.32, 17.31,
19.03, 21.43, 33.85) landed exactly on the five surviving whoosh and impact cues.
Pinned at 40 Mbps minimum so the 32.9 Mbps A-roll master is never the ceiling, and
the delivered cuts run 75 to 96 Mbps depending on the content. The other sources in
the film run 52.0 / 64.7 / 99.9 Mbps min / median / max, so parity with the A-roll
master alone would still leave the weakest link in the chain setting the quality.
These are Meta ads, not Instagram organic, so the Reels bottom UI band is not the
constraint it is elsewhere. And a markup box the client drew over the presenter's
own face was placement approval: they had already priced in the overlap, and
honouring the
drawn geometry beat re-deriving a safer placement nobody asked for.

note: Measured master bitrates in Mbps, for when the master file is not to hand. Pass one
with --master-bitrate. These are the CAMERA masters, not project transcodes.
